source.title: Single Image Unlearning: Efficient Machine Unlearning in Multimodal Large Language Models
source.authors: Jia-Qi Li; Qian-Shan Wei; Chuan-Yi Zhang; Gui-Lin Qi; Miaozeng Du; Yong-Rui Chen; Sheng Bi; Fan Liu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether prompting attacks recover unlearned visual recognition in MLLMs, using its own unlearning setup and jailbreak evaluations. This is a conceptual test of prompt-only recovery, not a direct reproduction of the original LLM unlearning methods.
record.gate_note: The paper tests multilingual and multi-hop jailbreak prompts after unlearning. Its MIA scores measure output similarity, not recovery of targeted knowledge, so they are recorded as findings that fit no version. It does not test recovery by relearning, activation edits or ablation, quantization, or a newer method resisting all listed attacks. The text's many qualitative multilingual examples are not exhaustively itemized; selected examples showing recovered target knowledge are included.
record.test_reason: New setting: unlearning visual recognition of concepts in an MLLM (LLaVA 7B/13B). The study measures post-unlearning target recognition and utility for SIU, PO, GA and GA+KL, then applies prompt-only attacks (multilingual and multi-hop). It also proposes SIU as a method robust to these prompt attacks, which bears on F for prompt attacks only. It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude SIU unlearns visual recognition from one image while preserving utility, and resists MIA and multilingual and multi-hop jailbreaks. They call GA+KL more vulnerable and self-contradictory, and say PO answers 'I do not know' and only learns the Q&A form. The record's 'problems' field is wrong that SIU's illustrated examples recover the target: those recoveries are GA+KL's or PO's.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces SIU for visual concept unlearning in MLLMs, using one training image and multifaceted fine-tuning data with dual-masked KL loss; also evaluates PO, GA and GA+KL baselines. It does not reproduce the cited LLM unlearning recipes as a recovery-attack study.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size changes SIU's reported EM generality from 99.0±0.0 for LLAVA7B to 90.0±0.8 for LLAVA13B. The paper reports different outcomes for multilingual and multi-hop prompts; language-specific examples vary.

fits_no_version.finding: Min-K% PROB-selected queries give ROUGE-L similarity to the original model's outputs of SIU 0.27, PO 0.32 and GA+KL 0.44. This is output similarity, not recovery of the target.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-similarity membership-inference scores rank unlearning methods but do not measure whether targeted knowledge is recoverable.

record.code_released: The paper says the code and benchmark will be released in the near future; no URL is stated.
record.problems: No model that never learned the target is used as a comparison, and no chance-level baseline is reported. The attack table gives no uncertainty estimates. Experiments train LLAVA only, as the authors note in the limitations. Some qualitative jailbreak examples recover the target even though the paper describes SIU as robust.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports further concept-wise results, fine-tuning-step plots, ablations, and simultaneous unlearning results in Figures 2–4 and Tables 2–3 and 6–7. They are not extracted because they do not test the prompt-only recovery conditions in the same direct way as the retained rows, or concern utility and method performance rather than a recovery attack. Most individual multilingual examples in Figures 12–14 are omitted; selected examples showing target recovery are retained.

untested.parts: No never-trained model or chance reference beyond the unseen-people output distribution (App. A.1). No pre-unlearning utility baseline. Relearning, quantization and internal attacks are not tried.
Not tested: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or internal analysis. Only output-probability (C-Dis) evidence for PO.
In-context information attacks are not tested. English rephrasing is folded into the Generality prompts rather than treated as an attack.
SIU is not tested against relearning, quantization, activation ablation or adaptive jailbreaks.

missing.what: PO answers affirming or naming Donald Trump under multilingual prompts (e.g., 'Ja, das ist ein Foto von Donald Trump', Russian 'Его зовут Дональд Трамп'). This contradicts the authors' statement that PO always says 'I do not know'.
PO's low C-Dis (0.4) and its plain-text answer, read as PO learning a refusal template rather than forgetting.
Baseline generality results for PO, GA and GA+KL. EM at 7B: 58.3, 36.3, 33.0. EM at 13B: 10.7, 24.7, 17.3. G-Eval at 13B: 4.6–4.8. GA specificity at 7B: 9.0.
GA+KL naming Trump in Japanese and Russian, and giving the Space Force fact under multi-hop prompting.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3 (MLLM visual-recognition setting). The figure text is column-interleaved in extraction. Attributions above follow the authors' statement that GA+KL names Trump in Chinese in Figs. 13–14, plus the content pattern (PO gives refusals or 'yes'; SIU gives invented names or 'no'). The Fig. 12 French and Russian column assignment remains uncertain. F is marked tested only for prompt attacks, because SIU is proposed as robust to jailbreaks.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison with a model that never learned the target, no chance-level reference, and no test of all listed recovery attacks. Targeted recognition is assessed with the paper's forgetting-oriented metrics, not a direct near-chance accuracy measure.
No post-unlearning recovery fine-tuning or relearning set.
No activation-direction ablation, internal edit recovery test, or analysis showing blocked access rather than deletion.
Tests multilingual and multi-hop jailbreak prompts, but not rephrasing alone, other-language prompts without jailbreak framing, or in-context information as separate conditions.
Does not test a newer method against the full set of attacks in the claim.
